plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with sample-cluster confound
plan.analytical_narrative: The data context reports 6 treated vs 6 control kidney samples with raw Salmon gene counts, no recorded processing batch, but a PCA that shows two clusters of six samples that split orthogonally to condition. This is the textbook signature of an unmodeled batch: a latent technical or biological factor is the dominant source of variance and, if untreated, either masks the condition effect or (more commonly) inflates false discoveries once dispersions are estimated on a design that ignores it. Because no batch variable was recorded, the plan cannot add a known covariate to the design (rule R-0022); instead it estimates surrogate variables directly from the counts with sva, using the condition as the known factor of interest, and adds those surrogate variables to the DESeq2 design alongside condition (rule R-0025/R-0068). The counts themselves are never adjusted or 'batch-corrected' prior to the test — only the design formula is extended — because adjusting counts before testing double-dips the batch information and produces overconfident p-values (R-0025). QC first establishes whether the two PCA clusters correspond to any recorded processing variable (none exists here) and whether any single sample is a stark outlier warranting investigation before modeling (R-0022, R-0034, R-0033). The DE test uses the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage on the standard raw-count pipeline: minimal low-count pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05 (R-0001, R-0002, R-0026, R-0009, R-0010). Because a suspected, unmodeled batch inflates test statistics and can make the p-value histogram look artificially strong, the plan explicitly inspects the p-value histogram after fitting with the surrogate variables and, if it remains irregular, re-estimates the null with fdrtool (R-0084, R-0083). A sensitivity run with the surrogate-variable design compared against a naive design (condition only) is reported so the difference the batch correction makes is visible, not asserted. Downstream, enrichment on the tested-gene universe follows only when the DE result exists: the knowledge-service check rejected a preranked fgsea/Hallmark call for this exact suspected-batch, n=6-per-group situation and named over-representation analysis with an explicit tested-gene universe as the permitted alternative, so the plan uses clusterProfiler ORA (Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways from the reference store) on the significant gene list with the tested genes as universe, per that ruling — with the caveat that if fewer than ~50 genes reach significance, ORA has little power and that must be stated in the report rather than papered over.
